text_en: And it came to pass, as I was going and drawing near to Damascus , at mid-day, that suddenly from heaven there shone round about me a great light:
text_la: Factum est autem, eunte me, et appropinquante Damasco media die, subito de cælo circumfulsit me lux copiosa:
text_pt: Ora, aconteceu que, indo eu já de caminho, e chegando perto de Damasco, quase ao meio-dia, de repente me rodeou uma grande luz do céu.

text_en: And falling on the ground, I heard a voice saying to me: Saul , Saul , why do you persecute me?
text_la: et decidens in terram, audivi vocem dicentem mihi : Saule, Saule, quid me persequeris?
text_pt: E caí por terra, e ouvi uma voz que me dizia: Saulo, Saulo, por que me persegues?

text_en: And I answered: Who are you, Lord? And he said to me: I am Jesus of Nazareth , whom you persecute .
text_la: Ego autem respondi : Quis es, domine? Dixitque ad me : Ego sum Jesus Nazarenus, quem tu persequeris.
text_pt: E eu respondi: Quem és, Senhor? E disse-me: Eu sou Jesus Nazareno, a quem tu persegues.

text_en: And they that were with me saw indeed the light: but they heard not the voice of him that spoke with me.
text_la: Et qui mecum erant, lumen quidem viderunt, vocem autem non audierunt ejus qui loquebatur mecum.
text_pt: E os que estavam comigo viram, em verdade, a luz, e se atemorizaram muito, mas não ouviram a voz daquele que falava comigo.

text_en: And I said: What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord said to me: Arise and go to Damascus ; and there it shall be told you of all things that you must do.
text_la: Et dixi : Quid faciam, domine? Dominus autem dixit ad me : Surgens vade Damascum : et ibi tibi dicetur de omnibus quæ te oporteat facere.
text_pt: Então disse eu: Senhor, que farei? E o Senhor disse-me: Levanta-te, e vai a Damasco, e ali se te dirá tudo o que te é ordenado fazer.

text_en: And whereas I did not see for the brightness of that light, being led by the hand by my companions, I came to Damascus ,
text_la: Et cum non viderem præ claritate luminis illius, ad manum deductus a comitibus, veni Damascum.
text_pt: E, como eu não via, por causa do esplendor daquela luz, fui levado pela mão dos que estavam comigo, e cheguei a Damasco.

text_en: and one Ananias, a man according to the law , having testimony of all the Jews who dwelt there,
text_la: Ananias autem quidam vir secundum legem, testimonium habens ab omnibus cohabitantibus Judæis,
text_pt: E um certo Ananias, homem piedoso conforme a lei, que tinha bom testemunho de todos os judeus que ali moravam,

text_en: coming to me and standing by me, said to me: Brother Saul , look up. And I, the same hour, looked upon him.
text_la: veniens ad me et astans, dixit mihi : Saule frater, respice. Et ego eadem hora respexi in eum.
text_pt: Vindo ter comigo, e apresentando-se, disse-me: Saulo, irmão, recobra a vista. E naquela mesma hora o vi.

text_en: But he said: The God of our fathers has preordained you that you should know his will and see the Just One and should hear the voice from his mouth.
text_la: At ille dixit : Deus patrum nostrorum præordinavit te, ut cognosceres voluntatem ejus, et videres justum, et audires vocem ex ore ejus:
text_pt: E ele disse: O Deus de nossos pais de antemão te designou para que conheças a sua vontade, e vejas aquele Justo e ouças a voz da sua boca.

text_en: For you shall be his witness to all men of those things which you have seen and heard.
text_la: quia eris testis illius ad omnes homines eorum quæ vidisti et audisti.
text_pt: Porque hás de ser sua testemunha para com todos os homens do que tens visto e ouvido.

text_en: And now why do you tarry? Rise up and be baptized and wash away your sins , invoking his name .
text_la: Et nunc quid moraris? Exsurge, et baptizare, et ablue peccata tua, invocato nomine ipsius.
text_pt: E agora por que te deténs? Levanta-te, e batiza-te, e lava os teus pecados, invocando o nome do Senhor.

text_en: And it came to pass, when I had come again to Jerusalem and was praying in the temple , that I was in a trance,
text_la: Factum est autem revertenti mihi in Jerusalem, et oranti in templo, fieri me in stupore mentis,
text_pt: E aconteceu que, tornando eu para Jerusalém, quando orava no templo, fui arrebatado para fora de mim.

text_en: and saw him saying unto me: Make haste and get you quickly out of Jerusalem : because they will not receive your testimony concerning me.
text_la: et videre illum dicentem mihi : Festina, et exi velociter ex Jerusalem : quoniam non recipient testimonium tuum de me.
text_pt: E vi aquele que me dizia: Dá-te pressa e sai apressadamente de Jerusalém; porque não receberão o teu testemunho acerca de mim.

text_en: And I said: Lord, they know that I cast into prison and beat in every synagogue them that believed in you.
text_la: Et ego dixi : Domine, ipsi sciunt quia ego eram concludens in carcerem, et cædens per synagogas eos qui credebant in te:
text_pt: E eu disse: Senhor, eles bem sabem que eu lançava na prisão e açoitava nas sinagogas os que criam em ti.

text_en: And when the blood of Stephen your witness was shed, I stood by and consented : and kept the garments of them that killed him.
text_la: et cum funderetur sanguis Stephani testis tui, ego astabam, et consentiebam, et custodiebam vestimenta interficientium illum.
text_pt: E quando o sangue de Estêvão, tua testemunha, se derramava, também eu estava presente, e consentia na sua morte, e guardava as capas dos que o matavam.

text_en: And he said to me: Go, for unto the Gentiles afar off will I send you.
text_la: Et dixit ad me : Vade, quoniam ego in nationes longe mittam te.
text_pt: E disse-me: Vai, porque hei de enviar-te aos gentios de longe.

text_en: And they heard him until this word and then lifted up their voice, saying: Away with such an one from the earth. For it is not fit that he should live.
text_la: Audiebant autem eum usque ad hoc verbum, et levaverunt vocem suam, dicentes : Tolle de terra hujusmodi : non enim fas est eum vivere.
text_pt: E ouviram-no até esta palavra, e levantaram a voz, dizendo: Tira da terra um tal homem, porque não convém que viva.

text_en: And as they cried out and threw off their garments and cast dust into the air,
text_la: Vociferantibus autem eis, et projicientibus vestimenta sua, et pulverem jactantibus in aërem,
text_pt: E, clamando eles, e arrojando de si as vestes, e lançando pó para o ar,
text_el: κραυγαζόντων τε αὐτῶν καὶ ῥιπτούντων τὰ ἱμάτια καὶ κονιορτὸν βαλλόντων εἰς τὸν ἀέρα,

text_en: the tribune commanded him to be brought into the castle, and that he should be scourged and tortured: to know for what cause they did so cry out against him.
text_la: jussit tribunus induci eum in castra, et flagellis cædi, et torqueri eum, ut sciret propter quam causam sic acclamarent ei.
text_pt: O tribuno mandou que o levassem para a fortaleza, dizendo que o examinassem com açoites, para saber por que causa assim clamavam contra ele.
text_el: ἐκέλευσεν ὁ χιλίαρχος εἰσάγεσθαι αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν, εἴπας μάστιξιν ἀνετάζεσθαι αὐτὸν ἵνα ἐπιγνῷ δι' ἣν αἰτίαν οὕτως ἐπεφώνουν αὐτῷ.

text_en: And when they had bound him with thongs, Paul says to the centurion that stood by him: Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman and uncondemned?
text_la: Et cum astrinxissent eum loris, dicit astanti sibi centurioni Paulus : Si hominem Romanum et indemnatum licet vobis flagellare?
text_pt: E, quando o estavam atando com correias, disse Paulo ao centurião que ali estava: É-vos lícito açoitar um romano, sem ser condenado?
text_el: ὡς δὲ προέτειναν αὐτὸν τοῖς ἱμᾶσιν εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν ἑστῶτα ἑκατόνταρχον ὁ Παῦλος: εἰ ἄνθρωπον Ῥωμαῖον καὶ ἀκατάκριτον ἔξεστιν ὑμῖν μαστίζειν;

text_en: Which the centurion hearing, went to the tribune and told him, saying: What are you about to do? For this man is a Roman citizen.
text_la: Quo audito, centurio accessit ad tribunum, et nuntiavit ei, dicens : Quid acturus es? hic enim homo civis Romanus est.
text_pt: E, ouvindo isto, o centurião foi, e anunciou ao tribuno, dizendo: Vê o que vais fazer, porque este homem é romano.
text_el: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης προσελθὼν τῷ χιλιάρχῳ ἀπήγγειλεν λέγων: τί μέλλεις ποιεῖν; ὁ γὰρ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος Ῥωμαῖός ἐστιν.

text_en: And the tribune coming, said to him: Tell me. Are you a Roman? But he said: Yea.
text_la: Accedens autem tribunus, dixit illi : Dic mihi si tu Romanus es? At ille dixit : Etiam.
text_pt: E, vindo o tribuno, disse-lhe: Dize-me, és tu romano? E ele disse: Sim.
text_el: προσελθὼν δὲ ὁ χιλίαρχος εἶπεν αὐτῷ: λέγε μοι, σὺ Ῥωμαῖος εἶ; ὁ δὲ ἔφη, ναί.

text_en: And the tribune answered: I obtained the being free of this city with a great sum. And Paul said: But I was born so.
text_la: Et respondit tribunus : Ego multa summa civilitatem hanc consecutus sum. Et Paulus ait : Ego autem et natus sum.
text_pt: E respondeu o tribuno: Eu com grande soma de dinheiro alcancei este direito de cidadão. Paulo disse: Mas eu o sou de nascimento.
text_el: ἀπεκρίθη δὲ ὁ χιλίαρχος: ἐγὼ πολλοῦ κεφαλαίου τὴν πολιτείαν ταύτην ἐκτησάμην. ὁ δὲ Παῦλος ἔφη: ἐγὼ δὲ καὶ γεγέννημαι.

text_en: Immediately therefore they departed from him that were about to torture him. The tribune also was afraid after he understood that he was a Roman citizen and because he had bound him.
text_la: Protinus ergo discesserunt ab illo qui eum torturi erant. Tribunus quoque timuit postquam rescivit, quia civis Romanus esset, et quia alligasset eum.
text_pt: E logo dele se apartaram os que o haviam de examinar; e até o tribuno teve temor, quando soube que era romano, visto que o tinha ligado.
text_el: εὐθέως οὖν ἀπέστησαν ἀπ' αὐτοῦ οἱ μέλλοντες αὐτὸν ἀνετάζειν: καὶ ὁ χιλίαρχος δὲ ἐφοβήθη ἐπιγνοὺς ὅτι Ῥωμαῖός ἐστιν καὶ ὅτι αὐτὸν ἦν δεδεκώς.

text_en: But on the next day, meaning to know more diligently for what cause he was accused by the Jews , he loosed him and commanded the priests to come together and all the council : and, bringing forth Paul , he set him before them.
text_la: Postera autem die volens scire diligentius qua ex causa accusaretur a Judæis, solvit eum, et jussit sacerdotes convenire, et omne concilium : et producens Paulum, statuit inter illos.
text_pt: E no dia seguinte, querendo saber ao certo a causa por que era acusado pelos judeus, soltou-o das prisões, e mandou vir o principais dos sacerdotes, e todo o seu conselho; e, trazendo Paulo, o apresentou diante deles.
text_el: Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον βουλόμενος γνῶναι τὸ ἀσφαλὲς τὸ τί κατηγορεῖται ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἔλυσεν αὐτόν, καὶ ἐκέλευσεν συνελθεῖν τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ πᾶν τὸ συνέδριον, καὶ καταγαγὼν τὸν Παῦλον ἔστησεν εἰς αὐτούς.

text_en: And Paul , looking upon the council , said: Men, brethren, I have conversed with all good conscience before God until this present day.
text_la: Intendens autem in concilium Paulus, ait : Viri fratres, ego omni conscientia bona conversatus sum ante Deum usque in hodiernum diem.
text_pt: E, pondo Paulo os olhos no conselho, disse: Homens irmãos, até ao dia de hoje tenho andado diante de Deus com toda a boa consciência.
text_el: ἀτενίσας δὲ Παῦλος τῷ συνεδρίῳ εἶπεν, ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ἐγὼ πάσῃ συνειδήσει ἀγαθῇ πεπολίτευμαι τῷ θεῷ ἄχρι ταύτης τῆς ἡμέρας.

text_en: And the high priest , Ananias, commanded them that stood by him to strike him on the mouth.
text_la: Princeps autem sacerdotum Ananias præcepit astantibus sibi percutere os ejus.
text_pt: Mas o sumo sacerdote, Ananias, mandou aos que estavam junto dele que o ferissem na boca.
text_el: ὁ δὲ ἀρχιερεὺς Ἁνανίας ἐπέταξεν τοῖς παρεστῶσιν αὐτῷ τύπτειν αὐτοῦ τὸ στόμα.

text_en: Then Paul said to him: God shall strike you, you whited wall. For, are you sitting to judge me according to the law and, contrary to the law , command me to be struck?
text_la: Tunc Paulus dixit ad eum : Percutiet te Deus, paries dealbate. Et tu sedens judicas me secundum legem, et contra legem jubes me percuti?
text_pt: Então Paulo lhe disse: Deus te ferirá, parede branqueada; tu estás aqui assentado para julgar-me conforme a lei, e contra a lei me mandas ferir?
text_el: τότε ὁ Παῦλος πρὸς αὐτὸν εἶπεν: τύπτειν σε μέλλει ὁ θεός, τοῖχε κεκονιαμένε: καὶ σὺ κάθῃ κρίνων με κατὰ τὸν νόμον, καὶ παρανομῶν κελεύεις με τύπτεσθαι;

text_en: And they that stood by said: Do you revile the high priest of God ?
text_la: Et qui astabant dixerunt : Summum sacerdotem Dei maledicis.
text_pt: E os que ali estavam disseram: Injurias o sumo sacerdote de Deus?
text_el: οἱ δὲ παρεστῶτες εἶπαν, τὸν ἀρχιερέα τοῦ θεοῦ λοιδορεῖς;

text_en: And Paul said: I knew not, brethren, that he is the high priest . For it is written: You shall not speak evil of the prince of your people.
text_la: Dixit autem Paulus : Nesciebam, fratres, quia princeps est sacerdotum. Scriptum est enim : Principem populi tui non maledices.
text_pt: E Paulo disse: Não sabia, irmãos, que era o sumo sacerdote; porque está escrito: Não dirás mal do príncipe do teu povo.
text_el: ἔφη τε ὁ Παῦλος, οὐκ ᾔδειν, ἀδελφοί, ὅτι ἐστὶν ἀρχιερεύς: γέγραπται γὰρ ὅτι ἄρχοντα τοῦ λαοῦ σου οὐκ ἐρεῖς κακῶς.

text_en: And Paul , knowing that the one part were Sadducees and the other Pharisees , cried out in the council : Men, brethren, I am a Pharisee , the son of Pharisees : concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.
text_la: Sciens autem Paulus quia una pars esset sadducæorum, et altera pharisæorum, exclamavit in concilio : Viri fratres, ego pharisæus sum, filius pharisæorum : de spe et resurrectione mortuorum ego judicor.
text_pt: E Paulo, sabendo que uma parte era de saduceus e outra de fariseus, clamou no conselho: Homens irmãos, eu sou fariseu, filho de fariseu; no tocante à esperança e ressurreição dos mortos sou julgado.
text_el: γνοὺς δὲ ὁ Παῦλος ὅτι τὸ ἓν μέρος ἐστὶν Σαδδουκαίων τὸ δὲ ἕτερον Φαρισαίων ἔκραζεν ἐν τῷ συνεδρίῳ, ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ἐγὼ Φαρισαῖός εἰμι, υἱὸς Φαρισαίων: περὶ ἐλπίδος καὶ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν κρίνομαι.

text_en: And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees . And the multitude was divided.
text_la: Et cum hæc dixisset, facta est dissensio inter pharisæos et sadducæos, et soluta est multitudo.
text_pt: E, havendo dito isto, houve dissensão entre os fariseus e saduceus; e a multidão se dividiu.
text_el: τοῦτο δὲ αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἐγένετο στάσις τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ Σαδδουκαίων, καὶ ἐσχίσθη τὸ πλῆθος.

text_en: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection , neither angel , nor spirit : but the Pharisees confess both.
text_la: Sadducæi enim dicunt non esse resurrectionem, neque angelum, neque spiritum : pharisæi autem utraque confitentur.
text_pt: Porque os saduceus dizem que não há ressurreição, nem anjo, nem espírito; mas os fariseus reconhecem uma e outra coisa.
text_el: Σαδδουκαῖοι γὰρ λέγουσιν μὴ εἶναι ἀνάστασιν μήτε ἄγγελον μήτε πνεῦμα, Φαρισαῖοι δὲ ὁμολογοῦσιν τὰ ἀμφότερα.

text_en: And there arose a great cry. And some of the Pharisees rising up, strove, saying: We find no evil in this man . What if a spirit has spoken to him, or an angel ?
text_la: Factus est autem clamor magnus. Et surgentes quidam pharisæorum, pugnabant, dicentes : Nihil mali invenimus in homine isto : quid si spiritus locutus est ei, aut angelus?
text_pt: E originou-se um grande clamor; e, levantando-se os escribas da parte dos fariseus, contendiam, dizendo: Nenhum mal achamos neste homem, e, se algum espírito ou anjo lhe falou, não lutemos contra Deus.
text_el: ἐγένετο δὲ κραυγὴ μεγάλη, καὶ ἀναστάντες τινὲς τῶν γραμματέων τοῦ μέρους τῶν Φαρισαίων διεμάχοντο λέγοντες, οὐδὲν κακὸν εὑρίσκομεν ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τούτῳ: εἰ δὲ πνεῦμα ἐλάλησεν αὐτῷ ἢ ἄγγελος

text_en: And when there arose a great dissension, the tribune, fearing lest Paul should be pulled in pieces by them, commanded the soldiers to go down and to take him by force from among them and to bring him into the castle.
text_la: Et cum magna dissensio facta esset, timens tribunus ne discerperetur Paulus ab ipsis, jussit milites descendere, et rapere eum de medio eorum, ac deducere eum in castra.
text_pt: E, havendo grande dissensão, o tribuno, temendo que Paulo fosse despedaçado por eles, mandou descer a soldadesca, para que o tirassem do meio deles, e o levassem para a fortaleza.
text_el: πολλῆς δὲ γινομένης στάσεως φοβηθεὶς ὁ χιλίαρχος μὴ διασπασθῇ ὁ Παῦλος ὑπ' αὐτῶν ἐκέλευσεν τὸ στράτευμα καταβὰν ἁρπάσαι αὐτὸν ἐκ μέσου αὐτῶν, ἄγειν εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν.

text_en: And the night following, the Lord standing by him, said: Be constant: for as you have testified of me in Jerusalem , so must you bear witness also at Rome .
text_la: Sequenti autem nocte assistens ei Dominus, ait : Constans esto : sicut enim testificatus es de me in Jerusalem, sic te oportet et Romæ testificari.
text_pt: E na noite seguinte, apresentando-se-lhe o Senhor, disse: Paulo, tem ânimo; porque, como de mim testificaste em Jerusalém, assim importa que testifiques também em Roma.
text_el: τῇ δὲ ἐπιούσῃ νυκτὶ ἐπιστὰς αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος εἶπεν: θάρσει: ὡς γὰρ διεμαρτύρω τὰ περὶ ἐμοῦ εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ, οὕτω σε δεῖ καὶ εἰς Ῥώμην μαρτυρῆσαι.

text_en: And when day had come, some of the Jews gathered together and bound themselves under a curse , saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they killed Paul .
text_la: Facta autem die collegerunt se quidam ex Judæis, et devoverunt, se dicentes neque manducaturos, neque bibituros donec occiderent Paulum.
text_pt: E, quando já era dia, alguns dos judeus fizeram uma conspiração, e juraram, dizendo que não comeriam nem beberiam enquanto não matassem a Paulo.
text_el: Γενομένης δὲ ἡμέρας ποιήσαντες συστροφὴν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἀνεθεμάτισαν ἑαυτοὺς, λέγοντες μήτε φαγεῖν μήτε πίειν ἕως οὗ ἀποκτείνωσιν τὸν Παῦλον.

text_en: And they were more than forty men that had made this conspiracy.
text_la: Erant autem plus quam quadraginta viri qui hanc conjurationem fecerant:
text_pt: E eram mais de quarenta os que fizeram esta conjuração.
text_el: ἦσαν δὲ πλείους τεσσεράκοντα οἱ ταύτην τὴν συνωμοσίαν ποιησάμενοι:

text_en: Who came to the chief priests and the ancients and said: We have bound ourselves under a great curse that we will eat nothing till we have slain Paul .
text_la: qui accesserunt ad principes sacerdotum et seniores, et dixerunt : Devotione devovimus nos nihil gustaturos, donec occidamus Paulum.
text_pt: E estes foram ter com os principais dos sacerdotes e anciãos, e disseram: Conjuramo-nos, sob pena de maldição, a nada provarmos até que matemos a Paulo.
text_el: οἵτινες προσελθόντες τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ τοῖς πρεσβυτέροις εἶπαν, ἀναθέματι ἀνεθεματίσαμεν ἑαυτοὺς μηδενὸς γεύσασθαι ἕως οὗ ἀποκτείνωμεν τὸν Παῦλον.

text_en: Now therefore do you with the council signify to the tribune, that he bring him forth to you, as if you meant to know something more certain touching him. And we, before he come near, are ready to kill him.
text_la: Nunc ergo vos notum facite tribuno cum concilio, ut producat illum ad vos, tamquam aliquid certius cognituri de eo. Nos vero priusquam appropiet, parati sumus interficere illum.
text_pt: Agora, pois, vós, com o conselho, rogai ao tribuno que vo-lo traga amanhã, como que querendo saber mais alguma coisa de seus negócios, e, antes que chegue, estaremos prontos para o matar.
text_el: νῦν οὖν ὑμεῖς ἐμφανίσατε τῷ χιλιάρχῳ σὺν τῷ συνεδρίῳ ὅπως καταγάγῃ αὐτὸν εἰς ὑμᾶς ὡς μέλλοντας διαγινώσκειν ἀκριβέστερον τὰ περὶ αὐτοῦ: ἡμεῖς δὲ πρὸ τοῦ ἐγγίσαι αὐτὸν ἕτοιμοί ἐσμεν τοῦ ἀνελεῖν αὐτόν.

text_en: Which when Paul's sister's son had heard, of their lying in wait, he came and entered into the castle and told Paul .
text_la: Quod cum audisset filius sororis Pauli insidias, venit, et intravit in castra, nuntiavitque Paulo.
text_pt: E o filho da irmã de Paulo, tendo ouvido acerca desta cilada, foi, e entrou na fortaleza, e o anunciou a Paulo.
text_el: Ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ υἱὸς τῆς ἀδελφῆς Παύλου τὴν ἐνέδραν παραγενόμενος καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὴν παρεμβολὴν ἀπήγγειλεν τῷ Παύλῳ.

text_en: And Paul , calling to him one of the centurions , said: Bring this young man to the tribune: for he has some thing to tell him.
text_la: Vocans autem Paulus ad se unum ex centurionibus, ait : Adolescentem hunc perduc ad tribunum, habet enim aliquid indicare illi.
text_pt: E Paulo, chamando a si um dos centuriões, disse: Leva este jovem ao tribuno, porque tem alguma coisa que lhe comunicar.
text_el: προσκαλεσάμενος δὲ ὁ Παῦλος ἕνα τῶν ἑκατονταρχῶν ἔφη, τὸν νεανίαν τοῦτον ἄπαγε πρὸς τὸν χιλίαρχον, ἔχει γὰρ ἀπαγγεῖλαί τι αὐτῷ.

text_en: And he, taking him, brought him to the tribune and said: Paul , the prisoner, desired me to bring this young man unto you, who has some thing to say to you.
text_la: Et ille quidem assumens eum duxit ad tribunum, et ait : Vinctus Paulus rogavit me hunc adolescentem perducere ad te, habentem aliquid loqui tibi.
text_pt: Tomando-o ele, pois, o levou ao tribuno, e disse: O preso Paulo, chamando-me a si, rogou-me que trouxesse este jovem, que tem alguma coisa para dizer-te.
text_el: ὁ μὲν οὖν παραλαβὼν αὐτὸν ἤγαγεν πρὸς τὸν χιλίαρχον καὶ φησίν, ὁ δέσμιος Παῦλος προσκαλεσάμενός με ἠρώτησεν τοῦτον τὸν νεανίαν ἀγαγεῖν πρὸς σέ, ἔχοντά τι λαλῆσαί σοι.

text_en: And the tribune, taking him by the hand, went aside with him privately and asked him: What is it that you have to tell me?
text_la: Apprehendens autem tribunus manum illius, secessit cum eo seorsum, et interrogavit illum : Quid est quod habes indicare mihi?
text_pt: E o tribuno, tomando-o pela mão, e pondo-se à parte, perguntou-lhe em particular: Que tens que me contar?
text_el: ἐπιλαβόμενος δὲ τῆς χειρὸς αὐτοῦ ὁ χιλίαρχος καὶ ἀναχωρήσας κατ' ἰδίαν ἐπυνθάνετο, τί ἐστιν ὃ ἔχεις ἀπαγγεῖλαί μοι;

text_en: And he said: The Jews have agreed to desire you that you would bring forth Paul tomorrow into the council , as if they meant to inquire some thing more certain touching him.
text_la: Ille autem dixit : Judæis convenit rogare te ut crastina die producas Paulum in concilium, quasi aliquid certius inquisituri sint de illo:
text_pt: E disse ele: Os judeus se concertaram rogar-te que amanhã leves Paulo ao conselho, como que tendo de inquirir dele mais alguma coisa ao certo.
text_el: εἶπεν δὲ ὅτι οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι συνέθεντο τοῦ ἐρωτῆσαί σε ὅπως αὔριον τὸν Παῦλον καταγάγῃς εἰς τὸ συνέδριον ὡς μέλλων τι ἀκριβέστερον πυνθάνεσθαι περὶ αὐτοῦ.

text_en: But do not give credit to them: for there lie in wait for him more than forty men of them, who have bound themselves by oath neither to eat nor to drink, till they have killed him. And they are now ready, looking for a promise from you.
text_la: tu vero ne credideris illis : insidiantur enim ei ex eis viri amplius quam quadraginta, qui se devoverunt non manducare, neque bibere donec interficiant eum : et nunc parati sunt, exspectantes promissum tuum.
text_pt: Mas tu não os creias; porque mais de quarenta homens de entre eles lhe andam armando ciladas; os quais se obrigaram, sob pena de maldição, a não comer nem beber até que o tenham morto; e já estão apercebidos, esperando de ti promessa.
text_el: σὺ οὖν μὴ πεισθῇς αὐτοῖς: ἐνεδρεύουσιν γὰρ αὐτὸν ἐξ αὐτῶν ἄνδρες πλείους τεσσεράκοντα, οἵτινες ἀνεθεμάτισαν ἑαυτοὺς μήτε φαγεῖν μήτε πιεῖν ἕως οὗ ἀνέλωσιν αὐτόν, καὶ νῦν εἰσιν ἕτοιμοι προσδεχόμενοι τὴν ἀπὸ σοῦ ἐπαγγελίαν.

text_en: The tribune therefore dismissed the young man, charging him that he should tell no man that he had made known these things unto him.
text_la: Tribunus igitur dimisit adolescentem, præcipiens ne cui loqueretur quoniam hæc nota sibi fecisset.
text_pt: Então o tribuno despediu o jovem, mandando-lhe que a ninguém dissesse que lhe havia contado aquilo.
text_el: ὁ μὲν οὖν χιλίαρχος ἀπέλυσε τὸν νεανίσκον παραγγείλας μηδενὶ ἐκλαλῆσαι ὅτι ταῦτα ἐνεφάνισας πρός ἐμέ.

text_en: Then having called two centurions , he said to them: Make ready two hundred soldiers to go as far as Caesarea : and seventy horsemen and two hundred spearmen, for the third hour of the night.
text_la: Et vocatis duobus centurionibus, dixit illis : Parate milites ducentos ut eant usque Cæsaream, et equites septuaginta, et lancearios ducentos a tertia hora noctis,
text_pt: E, chamando dois centuriões, lhes disse: Aprontai para as três horas da noite duzentos soldados, e setenta de cavalaria, e duzentos archeiros para irem até Cesaréia;
text_el: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τινὰς δύο τῶν ἑκατονταρχῶν εἶπεν, ἑτοιμάσατε στρατιώτας διακοσίους ὅπως πορευθῶσιν ἕως Καισαρείας, καὶ ἱππεῖς ἑβδομήκοντα καὶ δεξιολάβους διακοσίους, ἀπὸ τρίτης ὥρας τῆς νυκτός,

text_en: And provide beasts, that they may set Paul on and bring him safe to Felix the governor.
text_la: et jumenta præparate ut imponentes Paulum, salvum perducerent ad Felicem præsidem.
text_pt: E aparelhai animais, para que, pondo neles a Paulo, o levem salvo ao presidente Félix.
text_el: κτήνη τε παραστῆσαι ἵνα ἐπιβιβάσαντες τὸν Παῦλον διασώσωσι πρὸς Φήλικα τὸν ἡγεμόνα,

text_en: (For he feared lest perhaps the Jews might take him away by force and kill him: and he should afterwards be slandered , as if he was to take money.) And he wrote a letter after this manner:
text_la: (Timuit enim ne forte raperent eum Judæi, et occiderent, et ipse postea calumniam sustineret, tamquam accepturus pecuniam.)
text_pt: E escreveu uma carta, que continha isto:
text_el: γράψας ἐπιστολὴν ἔχουσαν τὸν τύπον τοῦτον:

text_en: Claudius Lysias to the most excellent governor, Felix, greeting:
text_la: Scribens epistolam continentem hæc : Claudius Lysias optimo præsidi Felici, salutem.
text_pt: Cláudio Lísias, a Félix, potentíssimo presidente, saúde.
text_el: Κλαύδιος Λυσίας τῷ κρατίστῳ ἡγεμόνι Φήλικι χαίρειν.

text_en: This man , being taken by the Jews and ready to be killed by them, I rescued, coming in with an army, understanding that he is a Roman.
text_la: Virum hunc comprehensum a Judæis, et incipientem interfici ab eis, superveniens cum exercitu eripui, cognito quia Romanus est.
text_pt: Esse homem foi preso pelos judeus; e, estando já a ponto de ser morto por eles, sobrevim eu com a soldadesca, e o livrei, informado de que era romano.
text_el: τὸν ἄνδρα τοῦτον συλλημφθέντα ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ μέλλοντα ἀναιρεῖσθαι ὑπ' αὐτῶν ἐπιστὰς σὺν τῷ στρατεύματι ἐξειλάμην, μαθὼν ὅτι Ῥωμαῖός ἐστιν:

text_en: And meaning to know the cause which they objected unto him, I brought him forth into their council .
text_la: Volensque scire causam quam objiciebant illi, deduxi eum in concilium eorum.
text_pt: E, querendo saber a causa por que o acusavam, o levei ao seu conselho.
text_el: βουλόμενός τε ἐπιγνῶναι τὴν αἰτίαν δι' ἣν ἐνεκάλουν αὐτῷ [κατήγαγον εἰς τὸ συνέδριον αὐτῶν]:

text_en: Whom I found to be accused concerning questions of their law ; but having nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bands.
text_la: Quem inveni accusari de quæstionibus legis ipsorum, nihil vero dignum morte aut vinculis habentem criminis.
text_pt: E achei que o acusavam de algumas questões da sua lei; mas que nenhum crime havia nele digno de morte ou de prisão.
text_el: ὃν εὗρον ἐγκαλούμενον περὶ ζητημάτων τοῦ νόμου αὐτῶν, μηδὲν δὲ ἄξιον θανάτου ἢ δεσμῶν ἔχοντα ἔγκλημα.

text_en: And when I was told of ambushes that they had prepared for him, I sent him to you, signifying also to his accusers to plead before you. Farewell.
text_la: Et cum mihi perlatum esset de insidiis quas paraverant illi, misi eum ad te, denuntians et accusatoribus ut dicant apud te. Vale.
text_pt: E, sendo-me notificado que os judeus haviam de armar ciladas a esse homem, logo to enviei, mandando também aos acusadores que perante ti digam o que tiverem contra ele. Passa bem.
text_el: μηνυθείσης δέ μοι ἐπιβουλῆς εἰς τὸν ἄνδρα ἔσεσθαι, ἐξαυτῆς ἔπεμψα πρὸς σέ, παραγγείλας καὶ τοῖς κατηγόροις λέγειν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐπὶ σοῦ.

text_en: Then the soldiers, according as it was commanded them, taking Paul , brought him by night to Antipatris .
text_la: Milites ergo secundum præceptum sibi assumentes Paulum, duxerunt per noctem in Antipatridem.
text_pt: Tomando, pois, os soldados a Paulo, como lhe fora mandado, o trouxeram de noite a Antipátride.
text_el: Οἱ μὲν οὖν στρατιῶται κατὰ τὸ διατεταγμένον αὐτοῖς ἀναλαβόντες τὸν Παῦλον ἤγαγον διὰ νυκτὸς εἰς τὴν Ἀντιπατρίδα:

text_en: And the next day, leaving the horsemen to go with him, they returned to the castle.
text_la: Et postera die dimissis equitibus ut cum eo irent, reversi sunt ad castra.
text_pt: E no dia seguinte, deixando aos de cavalo irem com ele, tornaram à fortaleza.
text_el: τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον ἐάσαντες τοὺς ἱππεῖς ἀπέρχεσθαι σὺν αὐτῷ ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν:

text_en: Who, when they had come to Caesarea and had delivered the letter to the governor, did also present Paul before him.
text_la: Qui cum venissent Cæsaream, et tradidissent epistolam præsidi, statuerunt ante illum et Paulum.
text_pt: Os quais, logo que chegaram a Cesaréia, e entregaram a carta ao presidente, lhe apresentaram Paulo.
text_el: οἵτινες εἰσελθόντες εἰς τὴν Καισάρειαν καὶ ἀναδόντες τὴν ἐπιστολὴν τῷ ἡγεμόνι παρέστησαν καὶ τὸν Παῦλον αὐτῷ.

text_en: And when he had read it and had asked of what province he was and understood that he was of Cilicia:
text_la: Cum legisset autem, et interrogasset de qua provincia esset, et cognoscens quia de Cilicia:
text_pt: E o presidente, lida a carta, perguntou de que província era; e, sabendo que era da Cilícia,
text_el: ἀναγνοὺς δὲ καὶ ἐπερωτήσας ἐκ ποίας ἐπαρχείας ἐστὶν καὶ πυθόμενος ὅτι ἀπὸ Κιλικίας,

text_en: I will hear you, said he, when your accusers come. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod's judgment hall.
text_la: Audiam te, inquit, cum accusatores tui venerint. Jussitque in prætorio Herodis custodiri eum.
text_pt: Disse: Ouvir-te-ei, quando também aqui vierem os teus acusadores. E mandou que o guardassem no pretório de Herodes.
text_el: διακούσομαί σου, ἔφη, ὅταν καὶ οἱ κατήγοροί σου παραγένωνται: κελεύσας ἐν τῷ πραιτωρίῳ τοῦ Ἡρῴδου φυλάσσεσθαι αὐτόν.

text_en: And after five days, the high priest , Ananias, came down with some ancients and one Tertullus, an orator, who went to the governor against Paul .
text_la: Post quinque autem dies descendit princeps sacerdotum Ananias, cum senioribus quibusdam, et Tertullo quodam oratore, qui adierunt præsidem adversus Paulum.
text_pt: E, cinco dias depois, o sumo sacerdote Ananias desceu com os anciãos, e um certo Tértulo, orador, os quais compareceram perante o presidente contra Paulo.
text_el: Μετὰ δὲ πέντε ἡμέρας κατέβη ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς Ἁνανίας μετὰ πρεσβυτέρων τινῶν καὶ ῥήτορος Τερτύλλου τινός, οἵτινες ἐνεφάνισαν τῷ ἡγεμόνι κατὰ τοῦ Παύλου.

text_en: And Paul being called for, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying: Whereas, through you we live in much peace and many things are rectified by your providence ,
text_la: Et citato Paulo cœpit accusare Tertullus, dicens : Cum in multa pace agamus per te, et multa corrigantur per tuam providentiam,
text_pt: E, sendo chamado, Tértulo começou a acusá-lo, dizendo: Visto como por ti temos tanta paz e por tua prudência se fazem a este povo muitos e louváveis serviços,
text_el: κληθέντος δὲ [αὐτοῦ] ἤρξατο κατηγορεῖν ὁ Τέρτυλλος λέγων, πολλῆς εἰρήνης τυγχάνοντες διὰ σοῦ καὶ διορθωμάτων γινομένων τῷ ἔθνει τούτῳ διὰ τῆς σῆς προνοίας,

text_en: we accept it always and in all places, most excellent Felix, with all thanksgiving.
text_la: semper et ubique suscipimus, optime Felix, cum omni gratiarum actione.
text_pt: Sempre e em todo o lugar, ó potentíssimo Félix, com todo o agradecimento o queremos reconhecer.
text_el: πάντῃ τε καὶ πανταχοῦ ἀποδεχόμεθα, κράτιστε Φῆλιξ, μετὰ πάσης εὐχαριστίας.

text_en: But that I be no further tedious to you, I desire you of your clemency to hear us in a few words.
text_la: Ne diutius autem te protraham, oro, breviter audias nos pro tua clementia.
text_pt: Mas, para que não te detenha muito, rogo-te que, conforme a tua eqüidade, nos ouças por pouco tempo.
text_el: ἵνα δὲ μὴ ἐπὶ πλεῖόν σε ἐγκόπτω, παρακαλῶ ἀκοῦσαί σε ἡμῶν συντόμως τῇ σῇ ἐπιεικείᾳ.

text_en: We have found this to be a pestilent man and raising seditions among all the Jews throughout the world: and author of the sedition of the sect of the Nazarenes .
text_la: Invenimus hunc hominem pestiferum, et concitantem seditiones omnibus Judæis in universo orbe, et auctorem seditionis sectæ Nazarenorum:
text_pt: Temos achado que este homem é uma peste, e promotor de sedições entre todos os judeus, por todo o mundo; e o principal defensor da seita dos nazarenos;
text_el: εὑρόντες γὰρ τὸν ἄνδρα τοῦτον λοιμὸν καὶ κινοῦντα στάσεις πᾶσιν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις τοῖς κατὰ τὴν οἰκουμένην πρωτοστάτην τε τῆς τῶν Ναζωραίων αἱρέσεως,

text_en: Who also has gone about to profane the temple : whom, we having apprehended, would also have judged according to our law .
text_la: qui etiam templum violare conatus est, quem et apprehensum voluimus secundum legem nostram judicare.
text_pt: O qual intentou também profanar o templo; e nós o prendemos, e conforme a nossa lei o quisemos julgar.
text_el: ὃς καὶ τὸ ἱερὸν ἐπείρασεν βεβηλῶσαι, ὃν καὶ ἐκρατήσαμεν,

text_en: But Lysias the tribune, coming upon us with great violence , took him away out of our hands;
text_la: Superveniens autem tribunus Lysias, cum vi magna eripuit eum de manibus nostris,
text_pt: Mas, sobrevindo o tribuno Lísias, no-lo tirou de entre as mãos com grande violência,

text_en: commanding his accusers to come to you. Of whom you may yourself, by examination, have knowledge of all these things whereof we accuse him.
text_la: jubens accusatores ejus ad te venire : a quo poteris ipse judicans, de omnibus istis cognoscere, de quibus nos accusamus eum.
text_pt: Mandando aos seus acusadores que viessem a ti; e dele tu mesmo, examinando-o, poderás entender tudo o de que o acusamos.
text_el: παρ' οὗ δυνήσῃ αὐτὸς ἀνακρίνας περὶ πάντων τούτων ἐπιγνῶναι ὧν ἡμεῖς κατηγοροῦμεν αὐτοῦ.

text_en: And the Jews also added and said that these things were so.
text_la: Adjecerunt autem et Judæi, dicentes hæc ita se habere.
text_pt: E também os judeus consentiam, dizendo serem estas coisas assim.
text_el: συνεπέθεντο δὲ καὶ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι φάσκοντες ταῦτα οὕτως ἔχειν.

text_en: Then Paul answered (the governor making a sign to him to speak): Knowing that for many years you have been judge over this nation, I will with good courage answer for myself.
text_la: Respondit autem Paulus (annuente sibi præside dicere) : Ex multis annis te esse judicem genti huic sciens, bono animo pro me satisfaciam.
text_pt: Paulo, porém, fazendo-lhe o presidente sinal que falasse, respondeu: Porque sei que já vai para muitos anos que desta nação és juiz, com tanto melhor ânimo respondo por mim.
text_el: Ἀπεκρίθη τε ὁ Παῦλος νεύσαντος αὐτῷ τοῦ ἡγεμόνος λέγειν, ἐκ πολλῶν ἐτῶν ὄντα σε κριτὴν τῷ ἔθνει τούτῳ ἐπιστάμενος εὐθύμως τὰ περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ ἀπολογοῦμαι,

text_en: For you may understand that there are yet but twelve days since I went up to adore in Jerusalem :
text_la: Potes enim cognoscere quia non plus sunt mihi dies quam duodecim, ex quo ascendi adorare in Jerusalem:
text_pt: Pois bem podes saber que não há mais de doze dias que subi a Jerusalém a adorar;
text_el: δυναμένου σου ἐπιγνῶναι ὅτι οὐ πλείους εἰσίν μοι ἡμέραι δώδεκα ἀφ' ἧς ἀνέβην προσκυνήσων εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ,

text_en: And neither in the temple did they find me disputing with any man or causing any concourse of the people: neither in the synagogues , nor in the city.
text_la: et neque in templo invenerunt me cum aliquo disputantem, aut concursum facientem turbæ, neque in synagogis, neque in civitate:
text_pt: E não me acharam no templo falando com alguém, nem amotinando o povo nas sinagogas, nem na cidade.
text_el: καὶ οὔτε ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ εὗρόν με πρός τινα διαλεγόμενον ἢ ἐπίστασιν ποιοῦντα ὄχλου οὔτε ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς οὔτε κατὰ τὴν πόλιν,

text_en: Neither can they prove unto you the things whereof they now accuse me.
text_la: neque probare possunt tibi de quibus nunc me accusant.
text_pt: Nem tampouco podem provar as coisas de que agora me acusam.
text_el: οὐδὲ παραστῆσαι δύνανταί σοι περὶ ὧν νυνὶ κατηγοροῦσίν μου.

text_en: But this I confess to you that according to the way which they call a heresy , so do I serve the Father and my God , believing all things which are written in the law and the prophets :
text_la: Confiteor autem hoc tibi, quod secundum sectam quam dicunt hæresim, sic deservio Patri et Deo meo, credens omnibus quæ in lege et prophetis scripta sunt:
text_pt: Mas confesso-te isto que, conforme aquele caminho que chamam seita, assim sirvo ao Deus de nossos pais, crendo tudo quanto está escrito na lei e nos profetas.
text_el: ὁμολογῶ δὲ τοῦτό σοι ὅτι κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ἣν λέγουσιν αἵρεσιν οὕτως λατρεύω τῷ πατρῴῳ θεῷ, πιστεύων πᾶσι τοῖς κατὰ τὸν νόμον καὶ τοῖς ἐν τοῖς προφήταις γεγραμμένοις,

text_en: Having hope in God , which these also themselves look for, that there shall be a resurrection of the just and unjust .
text_la: spem habens in Deum, quam et hi ipsi exspectant, resurrectionem futuram justorum et iniquorum.
text_pt: Tendo esperança em Deus, como estes mesmos também esperam, de que há de haver ressurreição de mortos, assim dos justos como dos injustos.
text_el: ἐλπίδα ἔχων εἰς τὸν θεόν, ἣν καὶ αὐτοὶ οὗτοι προσδέχονται, ἀνάστασιν μέλλειν ἔσεσθαι δικαίων τε καὶ ἀδίκων.

text_en: And herein do I endeavour to have always a conscience without offence, towards God and towards men .
text_la: In hoc et ipse studeo sine offendiculo conscientiam habere ad Deum et ad homines semper.
text_pt: E por isso procuro sempre ter uma consciência sem ofensa, tanto para com Deus como para com os homens.
text_el: ἐν τούτῳ καὶ αὐτὸς ἀσκῶ ἀπρόσκοπον συνείδησιν ἔχειν πρὸς τὸν θεὸν καὶ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους διὰ παντός.

text_en: Now after many years, I came to bring alms to my nation and offerings and vows .
text_la: Post annos autem plures eleemosynas facturus in gentem meam, veni, et oblationes, et vota,
text_pt: Ora, muitos anos depois, vim trazer à minha nação esmolas e ofertas.
text_el: δι' ἐτῶν δὲ πλειόνων ἐλεημοσύνας ποιήσων εἰς τὸ ἔθνος μου παρεγενόμην καὶ προσφοράς,

text_en: In which I was found purified in the temple : neither with multitude nor with tumult.
text_la: in quibus invenerunt me purificatum in templo : non cum turba, neque cum tumultu.
text_pt: Nisto me acharam já santificado no templo, não em ajuntamentos, nem com alvoroços, uns certos judeus da Ásia,
text_el: ἐν αἷς εὗρόν με ἡγνισμένον ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ, οὐ μετὰ ὄχλου οὐδὲ μετὰ θορύβου:

text_en: But certain Jews of Asia , who ought to be present before you and to accuse, if they had anything against me:
text_la: Quidam autem ex Asia Judæi, quos oportebat apud te præsto esse, et accusare si quid haberent adversum me:
text_pt: Os quais convinha que estivessem presentes perante ti, e me acusassem, se alguma coisa contra mim tivessem.
text_el: τινὲς δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἀσίας Ἰουδαῖοι, οὓς ἔδει ἐπὶ σοῦ παρεῖναι καὶ κατηγορεῖν εἴ τι ἔχοιεν πρὸς ἐμέ.

text_en: Or let these men themselves say if they found in me any iniquity , when standing before the council ,
text_la: aut hi ipsi dicant si quid invenerunt in me iniquitatis cum stem in concilio,
text_pt: Ou digam estes mesmos, se acharam em mim alguma iniqüidade, quando compareci perante o conselho,
text_el: ἢ αὐτοὶ οὗτοι εἰπάτωσαν τί εὗρον ἀδίκημα στάντος μου ἐπὶ τοῦ συνεδρίου

text_en: except it be for this one voice only that I cried, standing among them: Concerning the resurrection of the dead am I judged this day by you.
text_la: nisi de una hac solummodo voce qua clamavi inter eos stans: Quoniam de resurrectione mortuorum ego judicor hodie a vobis.
text_pt: A não ser estas palavras que, estando entre eles, clamei: Hoje sou julgado por vós acerca da ressurreição dos mortos.
text_el: ἢ περὶ μιᾶς ταύτης φωνῆς ἧς ἐκέκραξα ἐν αὐτοῖς ἑστὼς ὅτι περὶ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν ἐγὼ κρίνομαι σήμερον ἐφ' ὑμῶν.

text_en: And Felix put them off, having most certain knowledge of this way, saying: When Lysias the tribune shall come down, I will hear you.
text_la: Distulit autem illos Felix, certissime sciens de via hac, dicens : Cum tribunus Lysias descenderit, audiam vos.
text_pt: Então Félix, havendo ouvido estas coisas, lhes pôs dilação, dizendo: Havendo-me informado melhor deste Caminho, quando o tribuno Lísias tiver descido, então tomarei inteiro conhecimento dos vossos negócios.
text_el: Ἀνεβάλετο δὲ αὐτοὺς ὁ Φῆλιξ, ἀκριβέστερον εἰδὼς τὰ περὶ τῆς ὁδοῦ εἴπας, ὅταν Λυσίας ὁ χιλίαρχος καταβῇ διαγνώσομαι τὰ καθ' ὑμᾶς,

text_en: And he commanded a centurion to keep him: and that he should be easy and that he should not prohibit any of his friends to minister unto him.
text_la: Jussitque centurioni custodire eum, et habere requiem, nec quemquam de suis prohibere ministrare ei.
text_pt: E mandou ao centurião que o guardasse em prisão, tratando-o com brandura, e que a ninguém dos seus proibisse servi-lo ou vir ter com ele.
text_el: διαταξάμενος τῷ ἑκατοντάρχῃ τηρεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ἔχειν τε ἄνεσιν καὶ μηδένα κωλύειν τῶν ἰδίων αὐτοῦ ὑπηρετεῖν αὐτῷ.

text_en: And after some days, Felix, coming with Drusilla his wife, who was a Jew , sent for Paul and heard of him the faith that is in Christ Jesus .
text_la: Post aliquot autem dies veniens Felix cum Drusilla uxore sua, quæ erat Judæa, vocavit Paulum, et audivit ab eo fidem quæ est in Christum Jesum.
text_pt: E alguns dias depois, vindo Félix com sua mulher Drusila, que era judia, mandou chamar a Paulo, e ouviu-o acerca da fé em Cristo.
text_el: Μετὰ δὲ ἡμέρας τινὰς παραγενόμενος ὁ Φῆλιξ σὺν Δρουσίλλῃ τῇ ἰδίᾳ γυναικὶ οὔσῃ Ἰουδαίᾳ μετεπέμψατο τὸν Παῦλον καὶ ἤκουσεν αὐτοῦ περὶ τῆς εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν πίστεως.

text_en: And as he treated of justice and chastity and of the judgment to come , Felix, being terrified , answered: For this time, go your way: but when I have a convenient time, I will send for you.
text_la: Disputante autem illo de justitia, et castitate, et de judicio futuro, tremefactus Felix, respondit : Quod nunc attinet, vade : tempore autem opportuno accersam te:
text_pt: E, tratando ele da justiça, e da temperança, e do juízo vindouro, Félix, espavorido, respondeu: Por agora vai-te, e em tendo oportunidade te chamarei.
text_el: διαλεγομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ περὶ δικαιοσύνης καὶ ἐγκρατείας καὶ τοῦ κρίματος τοῦ μέλλοντος ἔμφοβος γενόμενος ὁ Φῆλιξ ἀπεκρίθη, τὸ νῦν ἔχον πορεύου, καιρὸν δὲ μεταλαβὼν μετακαλέσομαί σε:

text_en: Hoping also withal that money should be given him by Paul : for which cause also oftentimes sending for him, he spoke with him.
text_la: simul et sperans quod pecunia ei daretur a Paulo, propter quod et frequenter accersens eum, loquebatur cum eo.
text_pt: Esperando ao mesmo tempo que Paulo lhe desse dinheiro, para que o soltasse; pelo que também muitas vezes o mandava chamar, e falava com ele.
text_el: ἅμα καὶ ἐλπίζων ὅτι χρήματα δοθήσεται [αὐτῷ] ὑπὸ τοῦ Παύλου: διὸ καὶ πυκνότερον αὐτὸν μεταπεμπόμενος ὡμίλει αὐτῷ.

text_en: But when two years were ended, Felix had for successor Portius Festus. And Felix being willing to show the Jews a pleasure, left Paul bound.
text_la: Biennio autem expleto, accepit successorem Felix Portium Festum. Volens autem gratiam præstare Judæis Felix, reliquit Paulum vinctum.
text_pt: Mas, passados dois anos, Félix teve por sucessor a Pórcio Festo; e, querendo Félix comprazer aos judeus, deixou a Paulo preso.
text_el: διετίας δὲ πληρωθείσης ἔλαβεν διάδοχον ὁ Φῆλιξ Πόρκιον Φῆστον: θέλων τε χάριτα καταθέσθαι τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ὁ Φῆλιξ κατέλιπε τὸν Παῦλον δεδεμένον.

text_en: Now when Festus had come into the province, after three days, he went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea .
text_la: Festus ergo cum venisset in provinciam, post triduum ascendit Jerosolymam a Cæsarea.
text_pt: Entrando, pois, Festo na província, subiu dali a três dias de Cesaréia a Jerusalém.
text_el: Φῆστος οὖν ἐπιβὰς τῇ ἐπαρχείᾳ μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἀνέβη εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἀπὸ Καισαρείας,

text_en: And the chief priests and principal men of the Jews went unto him against Paul : and they besought him,
text_la: Adieruntque eum principes sacerdotum et primi Judæorum adversus Paulum : et rogabant eum,
text_pt: E o sumo sacerdote e os principais dos judeus compareceram perante ele contra Paulo, e lhe rogaram,
text_el: ἐνεφάνισάν τε αὐτῷ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρῶτοι τῶν Ἰουδαίων κατὰ τοῦ Παύλου, καὶ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν

text_en: requesting favour against him, that he would command him to be brought to Jerusalem , laying wait to kill him in the way.
text_la: postulantes gratiam adversus eum, ut juberet perduci eum in Jerusalem, insidias tendentes ut interficerent eum in via.
text_pt: Pedindo como favor contra ele que o fizesse vir a Jerusalém, armando ciladas para o matarem no caminho.
text_el: αἰτούμενοι χάριν κατ' αὐτοῦ ὅπως μεταπέμψηται αὐτὸν εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ, ἐνέδραν ποιοῦντες ἀνελεῖν αὐτὸν κατὰ τὴν ὁδόν.

text_en: But Festus answered: That Paul was kept in Caesarea : and that he himself would very shortly depart thither.
text_la: Festus autem respondit servari Paulum in Cæsarea: se autem maturius profecturum.
text_pt: Mas Festo respondeu que Paulo estava guardado em Cesaréia, e que ele brevemente partiria para lá.
text_el: ὁ μὲν οὖν Φῆστος ἀπεκρίθη τηρεῖσθαι τὸν Παῦλον εἰς Καισάρειαν, ἑαυτὸν δὲ μέλλειν ἐν τάχει ἐκπορεύεσθαι:

text_en: Let them, therefore, says he, among you that are able, go down with me and accuse him, if there be any crime in the man .
text_la: Qui ergo in vobis, ait, potentes sunt, descendentes simul, si quod est in viro crimen, accusent eum.
text_pt: Os que, pois, disse, dentre vós, têm poder, desçam comigo e, se neste homem houver algum crime, acusem-no.
text_el: οἱ οὖν ἐν ὑμῖν, φησίν, δυνατοὶ συγκαταβάντες εἴ τί ἐστιν ἐν τῷ ἀνδρὶ ἄτοπον κατηγορείτωσαν αὐτοῦ.

text_en: And having tarried among them no more than eight or ten days, he went down to Caesarea . And the next day, he sat in the judgment seat and commanded Paul to be brought.
text_la: Demoratus autem inter eos dies non amplius quam octo aut decem, descendit Cæsaream, et altera die sedit pro tribunali, et jussit Paulum adduci.
text_pt: E, havendo-se demorado entre eles mais de dez dias, desceu a Cesaréia; e no dia seguinte, assentando-se no tribunal, mandou que trouxessem Paulo.
text_el: διατρίψας δὲ ἐν αὐτοῖς ἡμέρας οὐ πλείους ὀκτὼ ἢ δέκα, καταβὰς εἰς Καισάρειαν, τῇ ἐπαύριον καθίσας ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος ἐκέλευσεν τὸν Παῦλον ἀχθῆναι.

text_en: Who being brought, the Jews stood about him, who had come down from Jerusalem , objecting many and grievous causes, which they could not prove :
text_la: Qui cum perductus esset, circumsteterunt eum, qui ab Jerosolyma descenderant Judæi, multas et graves causas objicientes, quas non poterant probare:
text_pt: E, chegando ele, rodearam-no os judeus que haviam descido de Jerusalém, trazendo contra Paulo muitas e graves acusações, que não podiam provar.
text_el: παραγενομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ περιέστησαν αὐτὸν οἱ ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων καταβεβηκότες Ἰουδαῖοι, πολλὰ καὶ βαρέα αἰτιώματα καταφέροντες ἃ οὐκ ἴσχυον ἀποδεῖξαι,

text_en: Paul making answer for himself: Neither against the law of the Jews , nor against the temple , nor against Caesar , have I offended in anything.
text_la: Paulo rationem reddente : Quoniam neque in legem Judæorum, neque in templum, neque in Cæsarem quidquam peccavi.
text_pt: Mas ele, em sua defesa, disse: Eu não pequei em coisa alguma contra a lei dos judeus, nem contra o templo, nem contra César.
text_el: τοῦ Παύλου ἀπολογουμένου ὅτι οὔτε εἰς τὸν νόμον τῶν Ἰουδαίων οὔτε εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν οὔτε εἰς Καίσαρά τι ἥμαρτον.

text_en: But Festus, willing to show the Jews a pleasure, answering Paul , said: Will you go up to Jerusalem and there be judged of these things before me?
text_la: Festus autem volens gratiam præstare Judæis, respondens Paulo, dixit : Vis Jerosolymam ascendere, et ibi de his judicari apud me?
text_pt: Todavia Festo, querendo comprazer aos judeus, respondendo a Paulo, disse: Queres tu subir a Jerusalém, e ser lá perante mim julgado acerca destas coisas?
text_el: ὁ Φῆστος δὲ θέλων τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις χάριν καταθέσθαι ἀποκριθεὶς τῷ Παύλῳ εἶπεν, θέλεις εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἀναβὰς ἐκεῖ περὶ τούτων κριθῆναι ἐπ' ἐμοῦ;

text_en: Then Paul said: I stand at Caesar's judgment seat, where I ought to be judged. To the Jews I have done no injury, as you very well know .
text_la: Dixit autem Paulus : Ad tribunal Cæsaris sto : ibi me oportet judicari : Judæis non nocui, sicut tu melius nosti.
text_pt: Mas Paulo disse: Estou perante o tribunal de César, onde convém que seja julgado; não fiz agravo algum aos judeus, como tu muito bem sabes.
text_el: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Παῦλος: ἑστώς ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος Καίσαρος εἰμι, οὗ με δεῖ κρίνεσθαι. Ἰουδαίους οὐδὲν ἠδίκηκα, ὡς καὶ σὺ κάλλιον ἐπιγινώσκεις.

text_en: For if I have injured them or have committed anything worthy of death, I refuse not to die. But if there be none of these things whereof they accuse me, no man may deliver me to them. I appeal to Caesar .
text_la: Si enim nocui, aut dignum morte aliquid feci, non recuso mori : si vero nihil est eorum quæ hi accusant me, nemo potest me illis donare. Cæsarem appello.
text_pt: Se fiz algum agravo, ou cometi alguma coisa digna de morte, não recuso morrer; mas, se nada há das coisas de que estes me acusam, ninguém me pode entregar a eles; apelo para César.
text_el: εἰ μὲν οὖν ἀδικῶ καὶ ἄξιον θανάτου πέπραχά τι, οὐ παραιτοῦμαι τὸ ἀποθανεῖν: εἰ δὲ οὐδέν ἐστιν ὧν οὗτοι κατηγοροῦσίν μου, οὐδείς με δύναται αὐτοῖς χαρίσασθαι: Καίσαρα ἐπικαλοῦμαι.

text_en: Then Festus, having conferred with the council , answered: Have you appealed to Caesar ? To Caesar shall you go.
text_la: Tunc Festus cum concilio locutus, respondit : Cæsarem appellasti? ad Cæsarem ibis.
text_pt: Então Festo, tendo falado com o conselho, respondeu: Apelaste para César? para César irás.
text_el: τότε ὁ Φῆστος συλλαλήσας μετὰ τοῦ συμβουλίου ἀπεκρίθη, Καίσαρα ἐπικέκλησαι, ἐπὶ Καίσαρα πορεύσῃ.

text_en: And after some days, King Agrippa and Bernice came down to Caesarea , to salute Festus.
text_la: Et cum dies aliquot transacti essent, Agrippa rex et Bernice descenderunt Cæsaream ad salutandum Festum.
text_pt: E, passados alguns dias, o rei Agripa e Berenice vieram a Cesaréia, a saudar Festo.
text_el: Ἡμερῶν δὲ διαγενομένων τινῶν Ἀγρίππας ὁ βασιλεὺς καὶ Βερνίκη κατήντησαν εἰς Καισάρειαν ἀσπασάμενοι τὸν Φῆστον.

text_en: And as they tarried there many days, Festus told the king of Paul , saying: A certain man was left prisoner by Felix.
text_la: Et cum dies plures ibi demorarentur, Festus regi indicavit de Paulo, dicens : Vir quidam est derelictus a Felice vinctus,
text_pt: E, como ali ficassem muitos dias, Festo contou ao rei os negócios de Paulo, dizendo: Um certo homem foi deixado por Félix aqui preso,
text_el: ὡς δὲ πλείους ἡμέρας διέτριβον ἐκεῖ, ὁ Φῆστος τῷ βασιλεῖ ἀνέθετο τὰ κατὰ τὸν Παῦλον λέγων, ἀνήρ τίς ἐστιν καταλελειμμένος ὑπὸ Φήλικος δέσμιος,

text_en: About whom, when I was at Jerusalem , the chief priests and the ancients of the Jews came unto me, desiring condemnation against him.
text_la: de quo cum essem Jerosolymis, adierunt me principes sacerdotum et seniores Judæorum, postulantes adversus illum damnationem.
text_pt: Por cujo respeito os principais dos sacerdotes e os anciãos dos judeus, estando eu em Jerusalém, compareceram perante mim, pedindo sentença contra ele.
text_el: περὶ οὗ γενομένου μου εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἐνεφάνισαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι τῶν Ἰουδαίων, αἰτούμενοι κατ' αὐτοῦ καταδίκην:

text_en: To whom I answered: it is not the custom of the Romans to condemn any man , before that he who is accused have his accusers present and have liberty to make his answer, to clear himself of the things laid to his charge.
text_la: Ad quos respondi : Quia non est Romanis consuetudo damnare aliquem hominem priusquam is qui accusatur præsentes habeat accusatores, locumque defendendi accipiat ad abluenda crimina.
text_pt: Aos quais respondi não ser costume dos romanos entregar algum homem à morte, sem que o acusado tenha presentes os seus acusadores, e possa defender-se da acusação.
text_el: πρὸς οὓς ἀπεκρίθην ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν ἔθος Ῥωμαίοις χαρίζεσθαί τινα ἄνθρωπον πρὶν ἢ ὁ κατηγορούμενος κατὰ πρόσωπον ἔχοι τοὺς κατηγόρους τόπον τε ἀπολογίας λάβοι περὶ τοῦ ἐγκλήματος.

text_en: When therefore they had come hither, without any delay, on the day following, sitting in the judgment seat, I commanded the man to be brought.
text_la: Cum ergo huc convenissent sine ulla dilatione, sequenti die sedens pro tribunali, jussi adduci virum.
text_pt: De sorte que, chegando eles aqui juntos, no dia seguinte, sem fazer dilação alguma, assentado no tribunal, mandei que trouxessem o homem.
text_el: συνελθόντων οὖν ἐνθάδε ἀναβολὴν μηδεμίαν ποιησάμενος τῇ ἑξῆς καθίσας ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος ἐκέλευσα ἀχθῆναι τὸν ἄνδρα:

text_en: Against whom, when the accusers stood up, they brought no accusation of things which I thought ill of:
text_la: De quo, cum stetissent accusatores, nullam causam deferebant, de quibus ego suspicabar malum.
text_pt: Acerca do qual, estando presentes os acusadores, nenhuma coisa apontaram daquelas que eu suspeitava.
text_el: περὶ οὗ σταθέντες οἱ κατήγοροι οὐδεμίαν αἰτίαν ἔφερον ὧν ἐγὼ ὑπενόουν πονηρῶν,

text_en: But had certain questions of their own superstition against him, and of one Jesus deceased, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.
text_la: Quæstiones vero quasdam de sua superstitione habebant adversus eum, et de quodam Jesu defuncto, quem affirmabat Paulus vivere.
text_pt: Tinham, porém, contra ele algumas questões acerca da sua superstição, e de um tal Jesus, morto, que Paulo afirmava viver.
text_el: ζητήματα δέ τινα περὶ τῆς ἰδίας δεισιδαιμονίας εἶχον πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ περί τινος Ἰησοῦ τεθνηκότος, ὃν ἔφασκεν ὁ Παῦλος ζῆν.

text_en: I therefore being in a doubt of this manner of question, asked him whether he would go to Jerusalem and there be judged of these things.
text_la: Hæsitans autem ego de hujusmodi quæstione, dicebam si vellet ire Jerosolymam, et ibi judicari de istis.
text_pt: E, estando eu perplexo acerca da inquirição desta causa, disse se queria ir a Jerusalém, e lá ser julgado acerca destas coisas.
text_el: ἀπορούμενος δὲ ἐγὼ τὴν περὶ τούτων ζήτησιν ἔλεγον εἰ βούλοιτο πορεύεσθαι εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα κἀκεῖ κρίνεσθαι περὶ τούτων.

text_en: But Paul , appealing to be reserved unto the hearing of Augustus , I commanded him to be kept, till I might send him to Caesar .
text_la: Paulo autem appellante ut servaretur ad Augusti cognitionem, jussi servari eum, donec mittam eum ad Cæsarem.
text_pt: E, apelando Paulo para que fosse reservado ao conhecimento de Augusto, mandei que o guardassem até que o envie a César.
text_el: τοῦ δὲ Παύλου ἐπικαλεσαμένου τηρηθῆναι αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν τοῦ Σεβαστοῦ διάγνωσιν, ἐκέλευσα τηρεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ἕως οὗ ἀναπέμψω αὐτὸν πρὸς Καίσαρα.

text_en: And Agrippa said to Festus: I would also hear the man, myself. Tomorrow, said he, you shall hear him.
text_la: Agrippa autem dixit ad Festum : Volebam et ipse hominem audire. Cras, inquit, audies eum.
text_pt: Então Agripa disse a Festo: Bem quisera eu também ouvir esse homem. E ele disse: Amanhã o ouvirás.
text_el: Ἀγρίππας δὲ πρὸς τὸν Φῆστον, ἐβουλόμην καὶ αὐτὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀκοῦσαι. αὔριον, φησίν, ἀκούσῃ αὐτοῦ.

text_en: And on the next day, when Agrippa and Bernice had come with great pomp and had entered into the hall of audience with the tribunes and principal men of the city, at Festus' commandment, Paul was brought forth.
text_la: Altera autem die cum venisset Agrippa et Bernice cum multa ambitione, et introissent in auditorium cum tribunis et viris principalibus civitatis, jubente Festo, adductus est Paulus.
text_pt: E, no dia seguinte, vindo Agripa e Berenice, com muito aparato, entraram no auditório com os tribunos e homens principais da cidade, sendo trazido Paulo por mandado de Festo.
text_el: Τῇ οὖν ἐπαύριον ἐλθόντος τοῦ Ἀγρίππα καὶ τῆς Βερνίκης μετὰ πολλῆς φαντασίας καὶ εἰσελθόντων εἰς τὸ ἀκροατήριον σύν τε χιλιάρχοις καὶ ἀνδράσιν τοῖς κατ' ἐξοχὴν τῆς πόλεως, καὶ κελεύσαντος τοῦ Φήστου ἤχθη ὁ Παῦλος.

text_en: And Festus says: King Agrippa and all you men who are here present with us, you see this man , about whom all the multitude of the Jews dealt with me at Jerusalem , requesting and crying out that he ought not to live any longer.
text_la: Et dicit Festus : Agrippa rex, et omnes qui simul adestis nobiscum viri, videtis hunc de quo omnis multitudo Judæorum interpellavit me Jerosolymis, petentes et acclamantes non oportere eum vivere amplius.
text_pt: E Festo disse: Rei Agripa, e todos os senhores que estais presentes conosco; aqui vedes um homem de quem toda a multidão dos judeus me tem falado, tanto em Jerusalém como aqui, clamando que não convém que viva mais.
text_el: καί φησιν ὁ Φῆστος: Ἀγρίππα βασιλεῦ καὶ πάντες οἱ συμπαρόντες ἡμῖν ἄνδρες, θεωρεῖτε τοῦτον περὶ οὗ ἅπαν τὸ πλῆθος τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐνέτυχέν μοι ἔν τε Ἱεροσολύμοις καὶ ἐνθάδε, βοῶντες μὴ δεῖν αὐτὸν ζῆν μηκέτι.

text_en: Yet have I found nothing that he has committed worthy of death. But forasmuch as he himself has appealed to Augustus , I have determined to send him.
text_la: Ego vere comperi nihil dignum morte eum admisisse. Ipso autem hoc appellante ad Augustum, judicavi mittere.
text_pt: Mas, achando eu que nenhuma coisa digna de morte fizera, e apelando ele mesmo também para Augusto, tenho determinado enviar-lho.
text_el: ἐγὼ δὲ κατελαβόμην μηδὲν ἄξιον αὐτὸν θανάτου πεπραχέναι, αὐτοῦ δὲ τούτου ἐπικαλεσαμένου τὸν Σεβαστὸν ἔκρινα πέμπειν.

text_en: Of whom I have nothing certain to write to my lord. For which cause, I have brought him forth before you, and especially before you, O King Agrippa, that, examination being made, I may have what to write.
text_la: De quo quid certum scribam domino, non habeo. Propter quod produxi eum ad vos, et maxime ad te, rex Agrippa, ut interrogatione facta habeam quid scribam.
text_pt: Do qual não tenho coisa alguma certa que escreva ao meu senhor, e por isso perante vós o trouxe, principalmente perante ti, ó rei Agripa, para que, depois de interrogado, tenha alguma coisa que escrever.
text_el: περὶ οὗ ἀσφαλές τι γράψαι τῷ κυρίῳ οὐκ ἔχω: διὸ προήγαγον αὐτὸν ἐφ' ὑμῶν καὶ μάλιστα ἐπὶ σοῦ, βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα, ὅπως τῆς ἀνακρίσεως γενομένης σχῶ τί γράψω:

text_en: For it seems to me unreasonable to send a prisoner and not to signify the things laid to his charge.
text_la: Sine ratione enim mihi videtur mittere vinctum, et causas ejus non significare.
text_pt: Porque me parece contra a razão enviar um preso, e não notificar contra ele as acusações.
text_el: ἄλογον γάρ μοι δοκεῖ πέμποντα δέσμιον μὴ καὶ τὰς κατ' αὐτοῦ αἰτίας σημᾶναι.

text_en: Then Agrippa said to Paul : You are permitted to speak for yourself. Then Paul , stretching forth his hand, began to make his answer.
text_la: Agrippa vero ad Paulum ait : Permittitur tibi loqui pro temetipso. Tunc Paulus extenta manu cœpit rationem reddere:
text_pt: Depois Agripa disse a Paulo: É permitido que te defendas. Então Paulo, estendendo a mão em sua defesa, respondeu:
text_el: Ἀγρίππας δὲ πρὸς τὸν Παῦλον ἔφη: ἐπιτρέπεταί σοι ὑπὲρ σεαυτοῦ λέγειν. τότε ὁ Παῦλος ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἀπελογεῖτο,

text_en: I think myself happy , O King Agrippa, that I am to answer for myself this day before you, touching all the things whereof I am accused by the Jews .
text_la: De omnibus quibus accusor a Judæis, rex Agrippa, æstimo me beatum apud te cum sim defensurus me hodie,
text_pt: Tenho-me por feliz, ó rei Agripa, de que perante ti me haja hoje de defender de todas as coisas de que sou acusado pelos judeus;
text_el: περὶ πάντων ὧν ἐγκαλοῦμαι ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων, βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα, ἥγημαι ἐμαυτὸν μακάριον ἐπὶ σοῦ μέλλων σήμερον ἀπολογεῖσθαι,

text_en: Especially as you know all, both customs and questions, that are among the Jews . Wherefore I beseech you to hear me patiently.
text_la: maxime te sciente omnia, et quæ apud Judæos sunt consuetudines et quæstiones : propter quod obsecro patienter me audias.
text_pt: Mormente sabendo eu que tens conhecimento de todos os costumes e questões que há entre os judeus; por isso te rogo que me ouças com paciência.
text_el: μάλιστα γνώστην ὄντα σε πάντων τῶν κατὰ Ἰουδαίους ἐθῶν τε καὶ ζητημάτων: διὸ δέομαι μακροθύμως ἀκοῦσαί μου.

text_en: And my life indeed from my youth, which was from the beginning among my own nation in Jerusalem , all the Jews do know :
text_la: Et quidem vitam meam a juventute, quæ ab initio fuit in gente mea in Jerosolymis, noverunt omnes Judæi:
text_pt: Quanto à minha vida, desde a mocidade, como decorreu desde o princípio entre os da minha nação, em Jerusalém, todos os judeus a conhecem,
text_el: τὴν μὲν οὖν βίωσίν μου ἐκ νεότητος τὴν ἀπ' ἀρχῆς γενομένην ἐν τῷ ἔθνει μου ἔν τε Ἱεροσολύμοις ἴσασι πάντες Ἰουδαῖοι,

text_en: Having known me from the beginning (if they will give testimony) that according to the most sure sect of our religion I lived, a Pharisee .
text_la: præscientes me ab initio (si velint testimonium perhibere) quoniam secundum certissimam sectam nostræ religionis vixi pharisæus.
text_pt: Sabendo de mim desde o princípio (se o quiserem testificar), que, conforme a mais severa seita da nossa religião, vivi fariseu.
text_el: προγινώσκοντές με ἄνωθεν, ἐὰν θέλωσι μαρτυρεῖν, ὅτι κατὰ τὴν ἀκριβεστάτην αἵρεσιν τῆς ἡμετέρας θρησκείας ἔζησα Φαρισαῖος.

text_en: And now for the hope of the promise that was made by God to the fathers, do I stand subject to judgment:
text_la: Et nunc, in spe quæ ad patres nostros repromissionis facta est a Deo, sto judicio subjectus:
text_pt: E agora pela esperança da promessa que por Deus foi feita a nossos pais estou aqui e sou julgado.
text_el: καὶ νῦν ἐπ' ἐλπίδι τῆς εἰς τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν ἐπαγγελίας γενομένης ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ ἕστηκα κρινόμενος,

text_en: Unto which, our twelve tribes , serving night and day, hope to come. For which hope , O king, I am accused by the Jews .
text_la: in quam duodecim tribus nostræ nocte ac die deservientes, sperant devenire. De qua spe accusor a Judæis, rex.
text_pt: À qual as nossas doze tribos esperam chegar, servindo a Deus continuamente, noite e dia. Por esta esperança, ó rei Agripa, eu sou acusado pelos judeus.
text_el: εἰς ἣν τὸ δωδεκάφυλον ἡμῶν ἐν ἐκτενείᾳ νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν λατρεῦον ἐλπίζει καταντῆσαι: περὶ ἧς ἐλπίδος ἐγκαλοῦμαι ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων, βασιλεῦ.

text_en: Why should it be thought a thing incredible that God should raise the dead ?
text_la: Quid incredibile judicatur apud vos, si Deus mortuos suscitat?
text_pt: Pois quê? julga-se coisa incrível entre vós que Deus ressuscite os mortos?
text_el: τί ἄπιστον κρίνεται παρ' ὑμῖν εἰ ὁ θεὸς νεκροὺς ἐγείρει;

text_en: And I indeed did formerly think that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth .
text_la: Et ego quidem existimaveram me adversus nomen Jesu Nazareni debere multa contraria agere,
text_pt: Bem tinha eu imaginado que contra o nome de Jesus Nazareno devia eu praticar muitos atos;
text_el: ἐγὼ μὲν οὖν ἔδοξα ἐμαυτῷ πρὸς τὸ ὄνομα Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου δεῖν πολλὰ ἐναντία πρᾶξαι:

text_en: Which also I did at Jerusalem : and many of the saints did I shut up in prison , having received authority of the chief priests . And when they were put to death , I brought the sentence.
text_la: quod et feci Jerosolymis, et multos sanctorum ego in carceribus inclusi, a principibus sacerdotum potestate accepta : et cum occiderentur, detuli sententiam.
text_pt: O que também fiz em Jerusalém. E, havendo recebido autorização dos principais dos sacerdotes, encerrei muitos dos santos nas prisões; e quando os matavam eu dava o meu voto contra eles.
text_el: ὃ καὶ ἐποίησα ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις, καὶ πολλούς τε τῶν ἁγίων ἐγὼ ἐν φυλακαῖς κατέκλεισα, τὴν παρὰ τῶν ἀρχιερέων ἐξουσίαν λαβών, ἀναιρουμένων τε αὐτῶν κατήνεγκα ψῆφον,

text_en: And oftentimes punishing them, in every synagogue , I compelled them to blaspheme : and being yet more mad against them, I persecuted them even unto foreign cities.
text_la: Et per omnes synagogas frequenter puniens eos, compellebam blasphemare : et amplius insaniens in eos, persequebar usque in exteras civitates.
text_pt: E, castigando-os muitas vezes por todas as sinagogas, os obriguei a blasfemar. E, enfurecido demasiadamente contra eles, até nas cidades estranhas os persegui.
text_el: καὶ κατὰ πάσας τὰς συναγωγὰς πολλάκις τιμωρῶν αὐτοὺς ἠνάγκαζον βλασφημεῖν, περισσῶς τε ἐμμαινόμενος αὐτοῖς ἐδίωκον ἕως καὶ εἰς τὰς ἔξω πόλεις.

text_en: Whereupon, when I was going to Damascus with authority and permission of the chief priest ,
text_la: In quibus dum irem Damascum cum potestate et permissu principum sacerdotum,
text_pt: Sobre o que, indo então a Damasco, com poder e comissão dos principais dos sacerdotes,
text_el: Ἐν οἷς πορευόμενος εἰς τὴν Δαμασκὸν μετ' ἐξουσίας καὶ ἐπιτροπῆς τῆς τῶν ἀρχιερέων

text_en: at midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven , above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them that were in company with me.
text_la: die media in via vidi, rex, de cælo supra splendorem solis circumfulsisse me lumen, et eos qui mecum simul erant.
text_pt: Ao meio-dia, ó rei, vi no caminho uma luz do céu, que excedia o esplendor do sol, cuja claridade me envolveu a mim e aos que iam comigo.
text_el: ἡμέρας μέσης κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν εἶδον, βασιλεῦ, οὐρανόθεν ὑπὲρ τὴν λαμπρότητα τοῦ ἡλίου περιλάμψαν με φῶς καὶ τοὺς σὺν ἐμοὶ πορευομένους:

text_en: And when we were all fallen down on the ground, I heard a voice speaking to me in the Hebrew tongue : Saul , Saul , why do you persecute me? It is hard for you to kick against the goad.
text_la: Omnesque nos cum decidissemus in terram, audivi vocem loquentem mihi hebraica lingua : Saule, Saule, quid me persequeris? durum est tibi contra stimulum calcitrare.
text_pt: E, caindo nós todos por terra, ouvi uma voz que me falava, e em língua hebraica dizia: Saulo, Saulo, por que me persegues? Dura coisa te é recalcitrar contra os aguilhões.
text_el: πάντων τε καταπεσόντων ἡμῶν εἰς τὴν γῆν ἤκουσα φωνὴν λέγουσαν πρός με τῇ Ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ, Σαοὺλ Σαούλ, τί με διώκεις; σκληρόν σοι πρὸς κέντρα λακτίζειν.

text_en: And I said: Who are you, Lord? And the Lord answered: I am Jesus whom you persecute .
text_la: Ego autem dixi : Quis es, domine? Dominus autem dixit : Ego sum Jesus, quem tu persequeris.
text_pt: E disse eu: Quem és, Senhor? E ele respondeu: Eu sou Jesus, a quem tu persegues;
text_el: ἐγὼ δὲ εἶπα, τίς εἶ, κύριε; ὁ δὲ κύριος εἶπεν, ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὃν σὺ διώκεις.

text_en: But rise up and stand upon your feet: for to this end have I appeared to you, that I may make you a minister and a witness of those things which you have seen and of those things wherein I will appear to you,
text_la: Sed exsurge, et sta super pedes tuos : ad hoc enim apparui tibi, ut constituam te ministrum, et testem eorum quæ vidisti, et eorum quibus apparebo tibi,
text_pt: Mas levanta-te e põe-te sobre teus pés, porque te apareci por isto, para te pôr por ministro e testemunha tanto das coisas que tens visto como daquelas pelas quais te aparecerei ainda;
text_el: ἀλλὰ ἀνάστηθι καὶ στῆθι ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας σου: εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ ὤφθην σοι, προχειρίσασθαί σε ὑπηρέτην καὶ μάρτυρα ὧν τε εἶδές με ὧν τε ὀφθήσομαί σοι,

text_en: delivering you from the people and from the nations unto which now I send you:
text_la: eripiens te de populo et gentibus, in quas nunc ego mitto te,
text_pt: Livrando-te deste povo, e dos gentios, a quem agora te envio,
text_el: ἐξαιρούμενός σε ἐκ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἐθνῶν, εἰς οὓς ἐγὼ ἀποστέλλω σε

text_en: To open their eyes, that they may be converted from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God , that they may receive forgiveness of sins and a lot among the saints , by the faith that is in me.
text_la: aperire oculos eorum, ut convertantur a tenebris ad lucem, et de potestate Satanæ ad Deum, ut accipiant remissionem peccatorum, et sortem inter sanctos, per fidem quæ est in me.
text_pt: Para lhes abrires os olhos, e das trevas os converteres à luz, e do poder de Satanás a Deus; a fim de que recebam a remissão de pecados, e herança entre os que são santificados pela fé em mim.
text_el: ἀνοῖξαι ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν, τοῦ ἐπιστρέψαι ἀπὸ σκότους εἰς φῶς καὶ τῆς ἐξουσίας τοῦ Σατανᾶ ἐπὶ τὸν θεόν, τοῦ λαβεῖν αὐτοὺς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν καὶ κλῆρον ἐν τοῖς ἡγιασμένοις πίστει τῇ εἰς ἐμέ.

text_en: Whereupon, O King Agrippa, I was not incredulous to the heavenly vision .
text_la: Unde, rex Agrippa, non fui incredulus cælesti visioni:
text_pt: Por isso, ó rei Agripa, não fui desobediente à visão celestial.
text_el: ὅθεν, βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα, οὐκ ἐγενόμην ἀπειθὴς τῇ οὐρανίῳ ὀπτασίᾳ,

text_en: But to them first that are at Damascus and at Jerusalem , and unto all the country of Judea , and to the Gentiles did I preach, that they should do penance and turn to God , doing works worthy of penance .
text_la: sed his qui sunt Damasci primum, et Jerosolymis, et in omnem regionem Judææ, et gentibus, annuntiabam, ut pœnitentiam agerent, et converterentur ad Deum, digna pœnitentiæ opera facientes.
text_pt: Antes anunciei primeiramente aos que estão em Damasco e em Jerusalém, e por toda a terra da Judéia, e aos gentios, que se emendassem e se convertessem a Deus, fazendo obras dignas de arrependimento.
text_el: ἀλλὰ τοῖς ἐν Δαμασκῷ πρῶτόν τε καὶ Ἱεροσολύμοις, πᾶσάν τε τὴν χώραν τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἀπήγγελλον μετανοεῖν καὶ ἐπιστρέφειν ἐπὶ τὸν θεόν, ἄξια τῆς μετανοίας ἔργα πράσσοντας.

text_en: For this cause, the Jews , when I was in the temple , having apprehended me, went about to kill me.
text_la: Hac ex causa me Judæi, cum essem in templo, comprehensum tentabant interficere.
text_pt: Por causa disto os judeus lançaram mão de mim no templo, e procuraram matar-me.
text_el: ἕνεκα τούτων με Ἰουδαῖοι συλλαβόμενοι ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἐπειρῶντο διαχειρίσασθαι.

text_en: But being aided by the help of God , I stand unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying no other thing than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come to pass:
text_la: Auxilio autem adjutus Dei usque in hodiernum diem, sto, testificans minori atque majori, nihil extra dicens quam ea quæ prophetæ locuti sunt futura esse, et Moyses,
text_pt: Mas, alcançando socorro de Deus, ainda até ao dia de hoje permaneço dando testemunho tanto a pequenos como a grandes, não dizendo nada mais do que o que os profetas e Moisés disseram que devia acontecer,
text_el: ἐπικουρίας οὖν τυχὼν τῆς ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ ἄχρι τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης ἕστηκα μαρτυρόμενος μικρῷ τε καὶ μεγάλῳ, οὐδὲν ἐκτὸς λέγων ὧν τε οἱ προφῆται ἐλάλησαν μελλόντων γίνεσθαι καὶ Μωϋσῆς,

text_en: That Christ should suffer and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead and should show light to the people and to the Gentiles .
text_la: si passibilis Christus, si primus ex resurrectione mortuorum, lumen annuntiaturus est populo et gentibus.
text_pt: Isto é, que o Cristo devia padecer, e sendo o primeiro da ressurreição dentre os mortos, devia anunciar a luz a este povo e aos gentios.
text_el: εἰ παθητὸς ὁ Χριστός, εἰ πρῶτος ἐξ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν φῶς μέλλει καταγγέλλειν τῷ τε λαῷ καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν.

text_en: As he spoke these things and made his answer, Festus said with a loud voice: Paul , you are beside yourself: much learning does make you mad .
text_la: Hæc loquente eo, et rationem reddente, Festus magna voce dixit : Insanis, Paule : multæ te litteræ ad insaniam convertunt.
text_pt: E, dizendo ele isto em sua defesa, disse Festo em alta voz: Estás louco, Paulo; as muitas letras te fazem delirar.
text_el: ταῦτα δὲ αὐτοῦ ἀπολογουμένου ὁ Φῆστος μεγάλῃ τῇ φωνῇ φησιν: μαίνῃ, Παῦλε: τὰ πολλά σε γράμματα εἰς μανίαν περιτρέπει.

text_en: And Paul said: I am not mad , most excellent Festus, but I speak words of truth and soberness.
text_la: Et Paulus : Non insanio, inquit, optime Feste, sed veritatis et sobrietatis verba loquor.
text_pt: Mas ele disse: Não deliro, ó potentíssimo Festo; antes digo palavras de verdade e de um são juízo.
text_el: ὁ δὲ Παῦλος: οὐ μαίνομαι, φησίν, κράτιστε Φῆστε, ἀλλὰ ἀληθείας καὶ σωφροσύνης ῥήματα ἀποφθέγγομαι.

text_en: For the king knows of these things, to whom also I speak with confidence. For I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him. For neither was any of these things done in a corner.
text_la: Scit enim de his rex, ad quem et constanter loquor : latere enim eum nihil horum arbitror. Neque enim in angulo quidquam horum gestum est.
text_pt: Porque o rei, diante de quem também falo com ousadia, sabe estas coisas, pois não creio que nada disto lhe é oculto; porque isto não se fez em qualquer canto.
text_el: ἐπίσταται γὰρ περὶ τούτων ὁ βασιλεύς, πρὸς ὃν παρρησιαζόμενος λαλῶ: λανθάνειν γὰρ αὐτὸν τούτων οὐ πείθομαι οὐθέν, οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ἐν γωνίᾳ πεπραγμένον τοῦτο.

text_en: Do you believe the prophets , O King Agrippa? I know that you believe .
text_la: Credis, rex Agrippa, prophetis? Scio quia credis.
text_pt: Crês tu nos profetas, ó rei Agripa? Bem sei que crês.
text_el: πιστεύεις, βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα, τοῖς προφήταις; οἶδα ὅτι πιστεύεις.

text_en: And Agrippa said to Paul : In a little you persuade me to become a Christian .
text_la: Agrippa autem ad Paulum : In modico suades me christianum fieri.
text_pt: E disse Agripa a Paulo: Por pouco me queres persuadir a que me faça cristão!
text_el: ὁ δὲ Ἀγρίππας πρὸς τὸν Παῦλον, ἐν ὀλίγῳ με πείθεις Χριστιανὸν ποιῆσαι.

text_en: And Paul said: I would to God that both in a little and in much, not only you, but also all that hear me this day, should become such as I also am, except these bands.
text_la: Et Paulus : Opto apud Deum, et in modico et in magno, non tantum te, sed etiam omnes qui audiunt hodie fieri tales, qualis et ego sum, exceptis vinculis his.
text_pt: E disse Paulo: Prouvera a Deus que, ou por pouco ou por muito, não somente tu, mas também todos quantos hoje me estão ouvindo, se tornassem tais qual eu sou, exceto estas cadeias.
text_el: ὁ δὲ Παῦλος, εὐξαίμην ἂν τῷ θεῷ καὶ ἐν ὀλίγῳ καὶ ἐν μεγάλῳ οὐ μόνον σὲ ἀλλὰ καὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀκούοντάς μου σήμερον γενέσθαι τοιούτους ὁποῖος καὶ ἐγώ εἰμι, παρεκτὸς τῶν δεσμῶν τούτων.

text_en: And the king rose up, and the governor and Bernice and they that sat with them.
text_la: Et exsurrexit rex, et præses, et Bernice, et qui assidebant eis.
text_pt: E, dizendo ele isto, levantou-se o rei, o presidente, e Berenice, e os que com eles estavam assentados.
text_el: ἀνέστη τε ὁ βασιλεὺς καὶ ὁ ἡγεμὼν ἥ τε Βερνίκη καὶ οἱ συγκαθήμενοι αὐτοῖς,

text_en: And when they had gone aside, they spoke among themselves, saying: This man has done nothing worthy of death or of bands.
text_la: Et cum secessissent, loquebantur ad invicem, dicentes : Quia nihil morte aut vinculis dignum quid fecit homo iste.
text_pt: E, apartando-se dali falavam uns com os outros, dizendo: Este homem nada fez digno de morte ou de prisões.
text_el: καὶ ἀναχωρήσαντες ἐλάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους λέγοντες ὅτι οὐδὲν θανάτου ἢ δεσμῶν ἄξιον πράσσει ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος.

text_en: And Agrippa said to Festus: This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed to Caesar .
text_la: Agrippa autem Festo dixit : Dimitti poterat homo hic, si non appellasset Cæsarem.
text_pt: E Agripa disse a Festo: Bem podia soltar-se este homem, se não houvera apelado para César.
text_el: Ἀγρίππας δὲ τῷ Φήστῳ ἔφη: ἀπολελύσθαι ἐδύνατο ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος εἰ μὴ ἐπεκέκλητο Καίσαρα.

text_en: And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto {one} named Julius, a centurion of Augustus' band.
text_pt: E, como se determinou que havíamos de navegar para a Itália, entregaram Paulo, e alguns outros presos, a um centurião por nome Júlio, da coorte augusta.
text_el: Ὡς δὲ ἐκρίθη τοῦ ἀποπλεῖν ἡμᾶς εἰς τὴν Ἰταλίαν, παρεδίδουν τόν τε Παῦλον καί τινας ἑτέρους δεσμώτας ἑκατοντάρχῃ ὀνόματι Ἰουλίῳ σπείρης Σεβαστῆς.

text_en: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; {one} Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
text_pt: E, embarcando nós em um navio adramitino, partimos navegando pelos lugares da costa da Ásia, estando conosco Aristarco, macedônio, de Tessalônica.
text_el: ἐπιβάντες δὲ πλοίῳ Ἀδραμυττηνῷ μέλλοντι πλεῖν εἰς τοὺς κατὰ τὴν Ἀσίαν τόπους ἀνήχθημεν, ὄντος σὺν ἡμῖν Ἀριστάρχου Μακεδόνος Θεσσαλονικέως:

text_en: And the next {day} we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave {him} liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself.
text_pt: E chegamos no dia seguinte a Sidom, e Júlio, tratando Paulo humanamente, lhe permitiu ir ver os amigos, para que cuidassem dele.
text_el: τῇ τε ἑτέρᾳ κατήχθημεν εἰς Σιδῶνα, φιλανθρώπως τε ὁ Ἰούλιος τῷ Παύλῳ χρησάμενος ἐπέτρεψεν πρὸς τοὺς φίλους πορευθέντι ἐπιμελείας τυχεῖν.

text_en: And when we had launched from thence, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
text_pt: E, partindo dali, fomos navegando abaixo de Chipre, porque os ventos eram contrários.
text_el: κἀκεῖθεν ἀναχθέντες ὑπεπλεύσαμεν τὴν Κύπρον διὰ τὸ τοὺς ἀνέμους εἶναι ἐναντίους,

text_en: And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, {a city} of Lycia.
text_pt: E, tendo atravessado o mar, ao longo da Cilícia e Panfília, chegamos a Mirra, na Lícia.
text_el: τό τε πέλαγος τὸ κατὰ τὴν Κιλικίαν καὶ Παμφυλίαν διαπλεύσαντες κατήλθομεν εἰς Μύρα τῆς Λυκίας.

text_en: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein.
text_pt: E, achando ali o centurião um navio de Alexandria, que navegava para a Itália, nos fez embarcar nele.
text_el: Κἀκεῖ εὑρὼν ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης πλοῖον Ἀλεξανδρῖνον πλέον εἰς τὴν Ἰταλίαν ἐνεβίβασεν ἡμᾶς εἰς αὐτό.

text_en: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, over against Salmone; {Crete: or, Candy}
text_pt: E, como por muitos dias navegássemos vagarosamente, havendo chegado apenas defronte de Cnido, não nos permitindo o vento ir mais adiante, navegamos abaixo de Creta, junto de Salmone.
text_el: ἐν ἱκαναῖς δὲ ἡμέραις βραδυπλοοῦντες καὶ μόλις γενόμενοι κατὰ τὴν Κνίδον, μὴ προσεῶντος ἡμᾶς τοῦ ἀνέμου, ὑπεπλεύσαμεν τὴν Κρήτην κατὰ Σαλμώνην,

text_en: And, hardly passing it, came unto a place which is called The fair havens; nigh whereunto was the city {of} Lasea.
text_pt: E, consteando-a dificilmente, chegamos a um lugar chamando Bons Portos, perto do qual estava a cidade de Laséia.
text_el: μόλις τε παραλεγόμενοι αὐτὴν ἤλθομεν εἰς τόπον τινὰ καλούμενον Καλοὺς Λιμένας, ᾧ ἐγγὺς ἦν πόλις Λασαία.

text_en: Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished {them}, {the fast: the fast was on the tenth day of the seventh month}
text_pt: E, passado muito tempo, e sendo já perigosa a navegação, pois, também o jejum já tinha passado, Paulo os admoestava,
text_el: ἱκανοῦ δὲ χρόνου διαγενομένου καὶ ὄντος ἤδη ἐπισφαλοῦς τοῦ πλοὸς διὰ τὸ καὶ τὴν νηστείαν ἤδη παρεληλυθέναι, παρῄνει ὁ Παῦλος

text_en: And said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage, not only of the lading and ship, but also of our lives. {hurt: or, injury}
text_pt: Dizendo-lhes: Senhores, vejo que a navegação há de ser incômoda, e com muito dano, não só para o navio e carga, mas também para as nossas vidas.
text_el: λέγων αὐτοῖς, ἄνδρες, θεωρῶ ὅτι μετὰ ὕβρεως καὶ πολλῆς ζημίας οὐ μόνον τοῦ φορτίου καὶ τοῦ πλοίου ἀλλὰ καὶ τῶν ψυχῶν ἡμῶν μέλλειν ἔσεσθαι τὸν πλοῦν.

text_en: Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul.
text_pt: Mas o centurião cria mais no piloto e no mestre, do que no que dizia Paulo.
text_el: ὁ δὲ ἑκατοντάρχης τῷ κυβερνήτῃ καὶ τῷ ναυκλήρῳ μᾶλλον ἐπείθετο ἢ τοῖς ὑπὸ Παύλου λεγομένοις.

text_en: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, {and there} to winter; {which is} an haven of Crete, and lieth toward the south west and north west.
text_pt: E, como aquele porto não era cômodo para invernar, os mais deles foram de parecer que se partisse dali para ver se podiam chegar a Fenice, que é um porto de Creta que olha para o lado do vento da África e do Coro, e invernar ali.
text_el: ἀνευθέτου δὲ τοῦ λιμένος ὑπάρχοντος πρὸς παραχειμασίαν οἱ πλείονες ἔθεντο βουλὴν ἀναχθῆναι ἐκεῖθεν, εἴ πως δύναιντο καταντήσαντες εἰς Φοίνικα παραχειμάσαι, λιμένα τῆς Κρήτης βλέποντα κατὰ λίβα καὶ κατὰ χῶρον.
